exact_prompt: Refine this exact existing adult watercolor illustration with one historically essential local correction. Preserve the entire composition, clerk's hand and wooden cancellation tool, folded cream letter, young Queen Victoria side-profile, black stamp color, red cancellation, copper coin, scissors, window, 1840s setting, brushwork, paper texture, dimensions and color palette. Change ONLY the outer paper silhouette of the small black postage stamp on the letter: its four outer edges must be perfectly straight, flat, scissor-cut sides with four simple square corners. It is an imperforate 1840 Penny Black. Remove every scallop, tooth, perforation, dotted hole and zigzag from all four sides. Leave a narrow perfectly smooth straight cream margin around the black portrait rectangle; no serration whatsoever. The fine ornamental engraving inside the black rectangle can remain, but the physical outside edge of the stamp must look like a plain tiny rectangle cut out by scissors. Do not add typography, dates, numbers, lettering, labels, logos, extra objects or any other change. This is a precise historical correction, not a redesign.

generation_history.prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

ARTICLE70: A historically appropriate 1840 British post-office counter still life, showing prepaid postage rather than a modern sticker or an unpaid letter. Main focal object is a folded cream letter bearing one small rectangular imperforate black stamp with a simplified youthful Queen Victoria side-profile; keep stamp edges straight, not perforated. A restrained red geometric cancellation crosses the stamp, with no letters, date or numbers. One natural adult clerk's hand gently lifts an ordinary wooden handstamp just after cancelling it. Supporting details are a plain pair of period scissors and a small unmarked copper penny coin on the wooden counter, referring to cutting early stamps and prepaid one-penny postage. No banknotes, modern envelope barcodes, written addresses, royal mail logos, stamp lettering or text anywhere, no plastic adhesive backing. The stamp is an intentionally simplified illustration, not a claimed philatelic facsimile. Calm close three-quarter view, warm ivory paper and sage-grey shadows with tiny black and muted-red accents, adult editorial watercolor, uncluttered and naturally drawn.
